Choosing among those is a decision the author would have made from the topic, and drafting would silently assert one. Section 8 compounds it: all ten samples address the same returning readership, so the profile records the distance to a regular and cannot tell me how this voice writes to a stranger or a hostile reader. To proceed I need the subject the piece is about, and — if it is not obvious from the subject — who is reading it and what the piece is for (an argument against a named actor, a set of steps for the reader to follow, or a personal account). An approximate length would also help, since every rate in the profile is per 1,000 words and the samples run 898 to 2,552.
